subtitle: Todd Barkan's 80th Birthday
why: Stanley Clarke and Lenny White reunite in an intimate club to celebrate Todd Barkan; a living link to Return to Forever and the history of Keystone Korner.
listen: Return to Forever — Romantic Warrior; Stanley Clarke — School Days

why: A master pianist whose swing, blues language and Jamaican rhythmic sensibility make this one of the warmest, most immediately enjoyable dates on the list.
High-level contemporary jazz-rock led by one of the defining drummers of fusion and progressive music.
Redman in a small club with Micah Thomas: modern acoustic jazz with a strong melodic center and serious improvisational depth.
Brazilian jazz at the scale it deserves: an intimate listening room, deep rhythmic language and decades of ensemble chemistry.

subtitle: Sounds From the Ancestors
why: A major living saxophonist connecting post-bop intensity with groove, gospel and African and Caribbean rhythmic ideas.

artist: Romero Lubambo + Chico Pinheiro + Diego Figueiredo
why: Three distinctive Brazilian guitar voices in one of the smallest major jazz rooms in the region — virtuosity with melody and rhythmic elegance.
listen: Romero Lubambo — Softly; Chico Pinheiro — City of Dreams

why: Victor, Regi, Roy and Joseph Wooten together: groove-heavy virtuosity crossing funk, jazz and fusion.
listen: Victor Wooten — A Show of Hands

why: A Chilean voice with a sophisticated jazz language and a natural Latin American sensibility; especially strong in an intimate room.
Modern Chilean jazz built around voice, guitar and songwriting rather than conventional standards.
One of the most technically startling young rhythm-and-keys partnerships in contemporary jazz, with strong fusion and experimental DNA.
A rare Japanese appearance that reframes traditional min’yō through cumbia, salsa, reggae and Afrobeat — culturally singular rather than simply virtuosic.
Dark folk, doom, industrial texture and a venue whose intimate acoustics should suit the ritual atmosphere of the music.
listen: She Reaches Out to She Reaches Out to She

subtitle: 85th Birthday Celebration
why: An 85th-birthday celebration for one of the architects of modern Afro-Cuban jazz — historical weight without leaving the DC area.
listen: Jazz Batá 2; Live at the Village Vanguard

subtitle: Adrian Belew · Tony Levin · Steve Vai · Terry Bozzio
venue: The Theater at MGM National Harbor
why: King Crimson’s 1980s language revisited by Belew and Levin with Steve Vai and Terry Bozzio — a concentration of progressive-rock history and virtuosity.
listen: King Crimson — Discipline; Beat; Three of a Perfect Pair

subtitle: Farewell Tour
why: A final chance to hear one of the defining boundary-crossing jazz groups of the last quarter century in a small club.
